newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia '97 c/a deficit at 11.5 bln rgt-Govt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia '97 c/a deficit at 11.5 bln rgt-Govt.

text.p: Malaysia's current account deficit is expected to narrow to 11.5 billion ringgit in 1997 from 14.8 billion in 1996 due to a larger surplus in the merchandise account, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
The government had earlier forecast a deficit of 17 billion ringgit for this year against 18.7 billion in 1995.
The improvement in the merchandise account will more than offset the increase in net payments on services, said the ministry's annual Economic Report, released ahead of the 1997 budget.

It said the services account deficit is expected to widen to 19.4 billion ringgit this year and to 21.5 billion in 1997 from 19.0 billion in 1995, due to higher outflows of investment income, payments for contract and professional charges and higher freight and insurance charges.
The merchandise account is projected to record a larger suplus of 4.6 billion ringgit in 1996 against 0.2 billion last year, due largely to a sharp decrease in import growth.
The 1996 current account deficit represents 6.3 percent of gross national product (GNP) against 9.0 percent of GNP in 1995, the report said.

The long-term capital account should record a lower net inflow of 12.4 billion ringgit in 1996 compared with 16.2 billion last year due to a higher level of investments abroad by Malaysians, increase in net payments by the government to reduce external borrowings and lower net external borrowings.
Thus, the basic balance -- the net position of the current and capital accounts -- will record a deficit of 2.4 billion ringgit in 1996 against a 2.5 billion ringgit deficit in 1995.
The overall balance of payments is expected to record a surplus of 1.2 billion ringgit against a deficit of 4.4 billion in 1995, the report said.

Consequently, the central bank's net international reserves are expected to increase by 1.2 billion ringgit to 65.0 billion ringgit at the end of 1996, sufficient to finance about 4.1 months of retained imports.
